about: Which lint covers which written rule, over which strings, and with which planted defect (proofs.mjs); what a lint cannot see is checked by hand, with the rows read and the result. check-copy.mjs (R1) reads this file, the guide and generated/proof-summary.json and fails when a rule, a § Errors item, a § Dates row, a § Step labels kind or a terminology row has no entry, when a named proof is missing or was not caught, or when a hand-checked population has changed since it was read. "over" names the strings a lint reads: new (every New string, B1 and its siblings), kept (every kept string and every source string no row touches, H17), source (every string in the source, H1), examples (the guide's own examples, F20), code (the code the checks read), data (the revision data), guide (the text of DESIGN.md).

new.note: lintString runs over every New string with its row's kind

kept.note: the same lints run over every kept string and kept row and every source string no row touches

source.note: lintSource runs over every string in the source and fails when one has no row

examples.note: lintString runs over the guide's own examples

manual.what: "three words where they fit" (TD-34) is a judgement about each label, so only the ceiling of five words is linted
manual.result: 11 of 11 need the extra words: 3 name a provider (Sign in with Google, Sign up with Google), 2 are a count and its noun (Approve 3 events), 1 is the person's own voice (I've copied the secret), 1 is two actions in one button (Sign in and allow access), 4 carry a qualifier that separates the button from its neighbour (Ask Kiwi to check, Go to your classes, Create first MCP server, Assign existing MCP servers); none can lose a word without losing its object

manual.what: "the consequence first, then permanence, then the way out" is a reading of each body (the lints catch the old patterns and H16 the title, the button and the permanence), so each body is read against the code that makes it true
manual.result: 20 read: 19 state what happens before whether it can be undone and each claim was checked against the code (DS.32 is the pattern's placeholder); one, A-09.09, promised permanence for a webhook that the backend only sets inactive (`webhooks/webhooks.service.ts:173-177`), and now says what happens and how to turn it on again

manual.what: "the first step, or who acts" and "names what was searched" are readings of each state (the lint catches "Nothing here" and "No … found")
manual.result: read in full: 0 say "Nothing here" or "No … found"; each is a "No {things} yet" or "No {things} match" state line (C5's one-clause form, for a secondary pane), a sentence that names the first step, or a sentence that says who acts and when; 0 defects

manual.what: "a helper adds information and never repeats the label" compares a helper with its field's label, which a string lint cannot see
manual.result: read in full, and each helper compared with the labels within 15 lines of its anchor by word overlap: 12 helper and label pairs overlap by 60% or more of the label's words (page descriptions that use the page title; a field's purpose beside its name), and in each the helper adds information beyond the label (a format, a default, a consequence or a purpose); 0 defects

manual.what: "a verb phrase naming its object, the same in the tooltip and the aria-label" needs the control, which a string lint cannot see (the first-letter lint, H9's every-copy rule and the repeated-row lint of lintSource cover what they can)
manual.result: read in full: 9 are the glyph's name "No value" (DS.54), the rest are verb phrases, the toolbar words the component tables name, or a tooltip that adds a sentence to a label that is already visible and so is not an icon's name (A-08.24 and A-08.78 on the approval chip, A-09.66 on the secret); 2 defects found and fixed, A-05.11 ("View details" in every row of the email table, now "View email details") and A-09.27 (a bare noun phrase, now "View delivery history")

manual.what: "nothing the page does not do" can only be checked against the code
manual.result: 36 rows that state what the product does were checked against the code they run, and the ones that say who can act against the access model on `fix/access-control`: 5 were corrected (A-09.09 promised that deleting a webhook can't be undone, and A-09.42, the dialog's title and its button and the row's control said delete, when the backend only sets the webhook inactive: they now say deactivate; A-09.66's tooltip now says only what the page does: it shows the secret once; A-14.26 said everything Kiwi learned from it, where the code removes the comments, the summaries, the search index and the stored file; A-12.10 sent every non-admin to an administrator for what a class's instructor may do under the model); 31 hold, S-01.07 once the branch merges (it ships with or after it, like S-05.06)

Anatomy..note: D9 (every error row cites C9) is built into the generator: composeError adds C9 to every error row, so a row cannot omit it

A batch is a partial result..note: H14 (every function that sends requests one after another has a partial-result row) reads the source's loops; its proof ran in round 4 and it is unchanged

manual.what: "students" for everyone is a reading of the audience of each string
manual.result: 46 read: 0 calls a mixed group students (the email recipients are the class roster's students; the mixed group is called users or the roster; the new caption of A-18.39 counts the students of one lecture, a role)

manual.what: "token" for both senses is a reading of each string (the lint catches "out of tokens")
manual.result: 34 read: 28 are the webhook's API token (a credential), 3 the model tokens of the analytics, 1 the model setting, 1 an OAuth token URL, 1 a design note about a model stream; 0 mixes the credential with the usage limit

examples.about: The guide's own samples (the voice attributes' in-range examples and the tone map's samples) hold to C16 like any string: each index row they quote is verified (a cite shows the code that makes what it says true), declared to claim nothing about the product (an instruction or the name of a control), or true only once a hand-off step is taken (a cite shows the gap and the hand-offs name the step). K1 finds the rows the samples quote; R1 fails on a quoted row that is in none of the three, on an entry no sample quotes any more, on a cite that does not resolve to a line of one file, and on a hand-off step the Voice section does not state.
